n: While Ammon teaches Lamoni’s people, the Spirit leads Aaron to the palace of Lamoni’s father, the king over all the land except Ishmael.
Aaron and his companions bow before the king and introduce themselves as Ammon’s brothers, whom he had released from prison.
They offer to be his servants. The king declines and asks them to teach him instead — Ammon’s generosity and words have troubled him — and asks why Ammon didn’t come.

f.w: the generosity and the greatness of the words

n: Aaron explains the Spirit sent Ammon to teach Lamoni’s people.

f.w: the Spirit of the Lord has called him another way

n: The king asks what Aaron means by “the Spirit of the Lord” — that is exactly what troubles him.

f.w: this is the thing which doth trouble me

n: He also asks what Ammon meant: repent and be saved, or be cast off at the last day.

f.w: cast off at the last day

n: Aaron asks if he believes in God. The king knows the Amalekites say there is one and has let them build sanctuaries — and if Aaron says there is a God, he will believe.

f.w: Believest thou that there is a God

n: Aaron rejoices and solemnly assures him there is a God.
The king asks: is God the Great Spirit who brought our fathers out of Jerusalem?
Yes, Aaron says — and he created all things in heaven and earth.
The king believes and asks Aaron to teach him everything.
Aaron reads the scriptures from Adam’s creation: man made in God’s image, given commandments, and fallen through transgression.

f.w: created man after his own image

n: He explains the Fall, humanity’s carnal state, and the plan of redemption prepared from the beginning through Christ.
Fallen man can’t earn salvation himself; Christ’s suffering and death atone for sins through faith and repentance. He breaks death’s bands, and the grave has no victory.

f.w: he could not merit anything of himself
the grave shall have no victory

n: The king asks how to receive eternal life and be born of God, with the wicked spirit rooted out of his heart. He would give up his entire kingdom for this joy.

f.w: What shall I do that I may have this eternal life

n: Aaron answers: bow before God, repent of all your sins, and call on him in faith, and you will receive the hope you seek.
The king kneels, then lies face down on the ground, and cries out mightily.
His prayer: “If there is a God… make thyself known unto me, and I will give away all my sins to know thee.” Then he collapses as if dead.

f.w: I will give away all my sins to know thee
f.g: One of the most quoted prayers in the Book of Mormon — he offers not his kingdom but his sins.

f.w: struck as if he were dead

n: Servants tell the queen. Seeing her husband lying lifeless with the Nephites standing by, she orders them killed.

f.g: A natural assumption given what she saw.

n: The servants refuse — they saw what happened and fear Aaron’s power, recalling stories of Ammon.

f.w: one of them is mightier than us all

n: Frightened herself, the queen calls the people to come and kill the missionaries.
To prevent a riot, Aaron reaches out, raises the king, and says “Stand.” The king stands with his strength restored.

f.w: raised the king from the earth

n: Witnessing this, the queen and servants marvel. The king teaches them, and his whole household is converted.
A crowd gathers at the queen’s command and begins grumbling against Aaron.
The king teaches the crowd and calms them.
He then has Aaron and his brothers preach to the crowd.

f.g: The king opens the door for the gospel.

n: The king sends a proclamation throughout his realm. Mormon pauses to describe geography: a narrow strip of wilderness running from sea to sea separated Lamanite lands from Zarahemla, past Manti and the head of the river Sidon.

f.g: A natural border between the two nations.

f.w: the head of the river Sidon

n: Many of the less settled Lamanites lived in tents in the western wilderness, including near Lehi’s first landing place by the seashore.
More Lamanites lived on the east coast. The Nephites were nearly surrounded but held the northern regions as far as the land Bountiful.

f.g: Not the same as Lehi’s Old World Bountiful (1 Nephi 17:5).

n: Bountiful bordered the land Desolation, the northern land once inhabited by the destroyed Jaredite people, whose bones Limhi’s explorers had found.
The northern land was called Desolation and the southern land Bountiful — a wilderness full of wild animals, some of which had migrated from the north.
Only a day and a half’s journey separated the east and west seas at the line between Bountiful and Desolation — a “small neck of land” connecting the land northward and southward.
The Nephites settled Bountiful from sea to sea and, with guards and armies, kept the Lamanites from overrunning the north.
This was strategic wisdom: it limited the Lamanites to the land of Nephi and preserved a northern refuge for the Nephites if needed.

f.w: a country whither they might flee

n: Mormon returns to the story of Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Himni, and their companions.
